clue.text: Rebuked by Conservative politician accepting a set scale

indicators.note: the politician's short label takes in the letter a, which lands between its two parts

parts.note: LIB is short for a Liberal, a politician
to rate someone is an old verb meaning to scold or berate them

explanation.surface: A politician scolded by a Tory colleague while agreeing to some fixed scale of pay.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Rebuked' looks like the past tense describing the politician, but it is RATED, to rate meaning to scold; it goes at the end even though it leads the clue.
explanation.definitionFit: To calibrate an instrument is to mark or adjust its graduations, so a calibrated gauge has had its scale set.

clue.text: Angler's target may be better across river

indicators.note: the word for outdoing spans the river letter, lying across it

parts.note: to cap something is to better or outdo it

explanation.surface: A fisherman's quarry might be improved by trying the far bank.
explanation.walkthrough: 'better' reads as an adjective but is the verb CAP, to outdo, which straddles R.
explanation.definitionFit: Coarse anglers fish for this freshwater species, so it is what an angler aims to hook.

clue.text: Criticises evening shifts covering degrees in management

indicators.note: the shifts word wraps round the degrees, covering them

parts.note: lates are late (evening) shifts at work
MBAs are Master of Business Administration degrees, taken in management

explanation.surface: A boss attacks the night-shift rota that covers people with business degrees.
explanation.walkthrough: 'shifts' looks like an anagram signal, but 'evening shifts' is one phrase, late shifts at work, split open by 'covering' round the business degrees.
explanation.definitionFit: To lambaste is to criticise harshly, a vivid synonym for censure.

clue.text: Crown at one time in support of bishop

indicators.note: in a down answer the lower word holds up the one above, supporting it

parts.note: B is the chess abbreviation for bishop
once means at one time, formerly

explanation.surface: A mitre or crown once worn to back up a bishop.
explanation.walkthrough: BONCE is British slang for the head, and 'crown' is the top of the head, not a royal headpiece.
explanation.definitionFit: Crown is the top of the head, and bonce is a British slang word for the head.

clue.text: Appeal to a non-drinker that's holding dray up

indicators.note: the teetotal letters enclose the reversed cart, holding it

parts.note: TT stands for teetotal, a non-drinker

indicators.note: in a down answer, up means the cart word is read from bottom to top

parts.note: a dray is a cart, traditionally a brewer's

explanation.surface: A temperance plea aimed at someone who has hoisted a brewer's cart.
explanation.walkthrough: 'up' reads the cart upwards in this down entry, and 'holding' puts that inside the teetotaller's letters; 'that's' is only a link.
explanation.definitionFit: To attract someone is to draw them in, the same as appealing to them.

clue.text: Wait to be given a lift, with the French beginning to supply food

indicators.note: in a down answer, lifting the word means reading it upwards

parts.note: to bide is to wait
le is French for the

indicators.note: only the opening letter of the next word is used

explanation.surface: Someone waits for a lift and gets a French meal to start.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to be given a lift' reads the waiting word upwards in this down entry, giving EDIB; 'with' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Edibles are things fit to eat, a plural noun for foodstuffs.

clue.text: Depressed, back following Romeo

indicators.note: back tells us to read the word for depressed backwards

parts.note: low means depressed or downcast
F is the abbreviation for following, as in page references

explanation.surface: Feeling down and then lagging behind a lover named Romeo.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Romeo' looks like the NATO alphabet R but is the definition: a ladies' man.
explanation.definitionFit: Both are slang for a womaniser, a man who chases women.

clue.text: Lyric poem about musical theatre

parts.note: an ode is a lyric poem
on means about, concerning

explanation.surface: A sung poem about a theatre that stages musicals.
explanation.walkthrough: The ancient Greek odeon was a roofed building for musical performance; the name lives on in cinemas.
explanation.definitionFit: In ancient Greece the odeon was a hall built for music and singing contests.

clue.text: Iris lost fluids freely if out

indicators.note: lost suggests letters gone astray, so the words are jumbled
out says the letters of if are to be taken away from the pool

explanation.surface: Someone named Iris lost a lot of fluid, if things got out of hand.
explanation.walkthrough: 'lost' mixes FLUIDS FREELY, and 'if out' removes I and F from the jumble; 'freely' is fodder, not the anagram signal.
explanation.definitionFit: The fleur-de-lys is a stylised iris, the heraldic flower of French royalty.

clue.text: Bounder in court without legal authority?

definitions.meaning: a ... moves by bounding, so is literally a bounder
a ... court is an unofficial tribunal with no legal authority

explanation.walkthrough: 'Bounder' looks like an old word for a cad, but means something that bounds.
explanation.definitionFit: The marsupial travels in leaps, and a kangaroo court is a sham trial lacking proper authority.

clue.text: King and country type (on paper)

parts.note: R is short for rex, Latin for king
Oman is a country in Arabia

explanation.surface: A monarch and a nation sorted into a category on paper.
explanation.walkthrough: 'type' is printing type, the upright typeface, not a kind of person.
explanation.definitionFit: Roman is the ordinary upright typeface used in print, as opposed to italic.

clue.text: Island people win at sea, moving with energy

indicators.note: moving suggests the letters shift around into a new order

parts.note: E is the physics symbol for energy

explanation.surface: Islanders win a sailing race, keeping it all energetic.
explanation.walkthrough: 'at sea' looks like the anagram signal but is part of the fodder; 'moving' is the signal.
explanation.definitionFit: Taiwanese are the inhabitants of Taiwan, an island off China.

clue.text: Spooner's greeting by friend getting post like this

indicators.note: Spooner's tells us to swap the opening sounds of the two words

parts.note: mate is British informal for a friend
a hail is a greeting or call

explanation.surface: A friendly greeting from a pal turns into abusive letters.
explanation.walkthrough: 'greeting by friend' gives MATE HAIL; swapping the starts gives the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Hate mail is abusive letters, a kind of post a recipient dreads.

clue.text: Fast mover adopting new hopeless case

indicators.note: the runner takes in the new letter, adopting it

parts.note: a goer is something fast

explanation.surface: A speedy runner takes on a lost cause.
explanation.definitionFit: A goner is someone beyond help, doomed or lost.

clue.text: Studied broadcast and initiated macho

indicators.note: broadcast means the word for studied is heard rather than seen

parts.note: read means studied, as in reading a subject at university
blooded means initiated, given a first experience

explanation.surface: A macho man studied, was on the airwaves, and got started.
explanation.walkthrough: READ in the past tense sounds like RED.
explanation.definitionFit: Red-blooded means vigorous and virile, close to macho in manly swagger.

clue.text: Picnics

parts.note: a picnicker dines outdoors, taking a meal outside rather than at home

explanation.walkthrough: The phrase usually means dining in a restaurant; here read literally, it means eating outdoors.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone on a picnic literally takes their meal outside.

clue.text: Take advantage of host concerned with check

parts.note: over means about or concerned with, as in fussing over
to stay is to check or halt

explanation.surface: A guest takes liberties with the host while worrying about a restraint.
explanation.walkthrough: 'host' is a person who receives guests; the reference is overstaying one's welcome.
explanation.definitionFit: A guest who stays too long imposes on the hospitality offered.

clue.text: Beastly affliction that is attached to dump

indicators.note: attached to says the abbreviation is joined on to the end of the dump word

parts.note: to scrap something is to dump it
i.e. abbreviates id est, that is

explanation.surface: A beast's illness, it seems, is found near the rubbish tip.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Beastly' here means of beasts, not nasty: the disease affects sheep.
explanation.definitionFit: Scrapie is a fatal brain disease of sheep and goats, an affliction of animals.

clue.text: Dance for soldiers with a heartless date?

parts.note: pro means for, in favour of
men are soldiers, as in officers and men

indicators.note: heartless removes the middle letters, leaving only the outer ones

explanation.surface: Is a ball for the troops with a date who has no feelings?
explanation.walkthrough: 'heartless date' reduces DATE to DE.
explanation.definitionFit: A promenade is a stately dance or ball, especially an American high-school prom.

clue.text: Be flexible, importing new set for a little lamb

indicators.note: the flexible word brings the reworked letters inside it

parts.note: to bend is to be flexible

indicators.note: new means the letters of set are arranged afresh

explanation.surface: Adapt by bringing in a new set, all for a small lamb.
explanation.walkthrough: 'new' rearranges the word set to EST. Best end is a British butcher's cut of lamb from the neck.
explanation.definitionFit: Best end of neck is a cut of lamb, so a portion of the meat.

clue.text: Rough sleeper should keep one written account

indicators.note: the sleeper word holds the numeral inside, keeping it

parts.note: a dosser is British slang for a homeless person sleeping rough
I is the Roman numeral one

explanation.surface: A homeless man ought to keep a written record.
explanation.definitionFit: A dossier is a file of documents giving a detailed record of a person or matter.

clue.text: Germany must be gutted after a game defence

indicators.note: the gutted country comes after the game in the answer

parts.note: polo is a game played on horseback

indicators.note: gutted removes the insides, leaving only the outer letters

explanation.surface: A German side, crushed after a match, must mount a defence.
explanation.walkthrough: 'gutted' strips GERMANY to GY. Apology here means apologia, a formal defence, not saying sorry.
explanation.definitionFit: An apology in the old sense is a reasoned defence of a belief or action, an apologia.

clue.text: Joined, contrary to expectation gripped by new date

indicators.note: the conjunction is held inside the rearranged date
new means the letters of date are rearranged

parts.note: but introduces something contrary to what was expected

explanation.surface: Married, against all expectation, with a new date set.
explanation.walkthrough: 'new' turns DATE into ATED, which grips BUT.
explanation.definitionFit: Things that abutted were adjacent, touching at a shared border, hence joined.

clue.text: Spring may see love unchanged

parts.note: love is zero in tennis, which looks like O
as is means unchanged, in the existing condition

explanation.surface: In springtime love may seem to stay the same.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Spring' looks like the season but is a water source.
explanation.definitionFit: An oasis is a fertile spot in the desert fed by a spring of water.

clue.text: Small and friendly crowd on the move

parts.note: S is the abbreviation for small, as in clothing sizes
warm means friendly or cordial

explanation.surface: A small, affable throng drifting along.
explanation.definitionFit: A swarm is a large moving mass of insects or people.

clue.text: Left after seeing country gent sheltering Republican hoard

indicators.note: the letter for left comes after the rest in the answer
the gent's word houses the party letter inside it

parts.note: a squire is a country landowner, a rural gentleman

explanation.surface: A rural gentleman shelters a Republican fugitive and then leaves with his stash.
explanation.walkthrough: 'hoard' is a verb, to squirrel away.
explanation.definitionFit: To squirrel things away is to hoard them, as squirrels store nuts.

clue.text: Promote review, lacking application

indicators.note: lacking means the word for application is taken away

parts.note: to appraise is to review or assess
an app is short for an application, as on a phone

explanation.surface: Give someone a step up after an assessment, though they lack diligence.
explanation.walkthrough: 'application' looks like diligence but is APP, removed from APPRAISE.
explanation.definitionFit: To raise someone is to promote them to a higher rank or pay.

clue.text: There's no end of danger in money drop

indicators.note: there's no says the letter that follows is missing from the money word

parts.note: bread is slang for money

indicators.note: end of takes only the last letter of danger

explanation.surface: No danger of a fall in cash values.
explanation.walkthrough: The last letter of 'danger' is R, which leaves BREAD.
explanation.definitionFit: A bead is a small drop of liquid, such as a bead of sweat.

clue.text: Short answer is in case of typecast writer

parts.note: a short is a small measure of spirits, a dram

indicators.note: is sits inside the casing letters
case of means only the outside letters, the casing

explanation.surface: A curt reply that sits in the typecast writer's corner.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Short' looks like an adjective but is a short measure of spirits, as served in a British pub.
explanation.definitionFit: A dramatist is a playwright, one kind of writer.

clue.text: Put a date on the setter's public face

parts.note: the setter is I, so the setter's (setter is) gives I'M
to age something is to give it a date

explanation.surface: The compiler fixes when to show his face in public.
explanation.definitionFit: A person's image is the impression they present to the world.

clue.text: Abuse rejected by a council that's elected

indicators.note: rejected means the word for abuse is turned back

parts.note: mud, as in slinging mud, is abuse or slander

explanation.surface: An elected body is rejected amid a hail of insults.
explanation.walkthrough: The Duma is the elected lower house of Russia's parliament.
explanation.definitionFit: The Duma is Russia's elected legislative assembly, a council of representatives.

clue.text: Positional advantage gained from game of cards with boss

parts.note: bridge is a card game
a head is a boss or leader

explanation.surface: Getting the upper hand by playing cards with one's employer.
explanation.definitionFit: A bridgehead is a foothold held on enemy ground, a military advantage of position.
